letters.to: The Grievance Redressal Officer, Sahyadri General Insurance Ltd. (fictional)
letters.subject: Request to re-assess cashless claim settlement - Policy NHP-2026-207731, Meera Krishnan, bill AMH/IP/26/20417
letters.body:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing about the cashless settlement of my claim for treatment at Aarogya Multispeciality Hospital from 21 Sep 2026 to 24 Sep 2026 (Laparoscopic appendectomy), bill no. AMH/IP/26/20417. Against a final bill of ₹1,33,540, ₹1,05,192 was approved and I was asked to pay ₹28,348.

I have compared the settlement with my policy wording, and the following deductions do not appear to be in line with the policy:

1. Co-payment applied that the policy doesn't require. The insurer deducted a 20% co-payment. For this claim (network, patient aged 41) the policy's co-payment is 0%. (Policy clause 3.2, Co-payment: "No co-payment applies to claims for treatment taken at a Network Hospital. A co-payment of 20% of the admissible claim amount applies to treatment taken at a Non-Network Hospital. An additional co-payment of 10%...") Amount: ₹26,528.

2. Covered item deducted as non-payable (bill line 13). The insurer treated line 13 Gloves and masks pack (₹1,150) as non-payable, but policy 3.4 (Consumables Benefit) makes these items payable during a covered hospitalisation. (Policy clause 3.4, Consumables Benefit: "Notwithstanding the list of non-payable items in Annexure II, non-medical items and consumables (including admission kits, gloves, masks and similar items) incurred during a covered hospitalisation are payable under...") Amount: ₹920.

I request that you re-assess the claim under the policy terms and release the additional ₹27,448, or explain in writing the policy basis for each deduction above.

This letter is a grievance under clause 5.2 (Grievances) of my policy. If it isn't resolved, I will escalate it as that clause provides.

Enclosed: final itemised hospital bill and settlement, policy schedule and wording, ClaimShield reconciliation report.

Yours faithfully,
Meera Krishnan
Policy no. NHP-2026-207731
[Phone] | [Email]

letters.to: The Billing Department, Aarogya Multispeciality Hospital, No. 18, Outer Ring Road, Marathahalli, Bengaluru 560037 (fictional)
letters.subject: Request for a corrected final bill - bill no. AMH/IP/26/20417, patient Meera Krishnan
letters.body:
Dear Billing Team,

I am writing about my final bill no. AMH/IP/26/20417 for treatment from 21 Sep 2026 to 24 Sep 2026. On going through the itemised bill, I found entries that I believe need correcting.

Please correct the following:

1. Room charged for more days than the stay (bill line 1). The stay was 3 nights but the room is billed for 4 days. The extra 1 day(s) come to ₹4,200. Amount: ₹4,200.

2. Inj. Ceftriaxone 1g: amount doesn't match quantity x rate (bill line 10). 8 units at ₹180 come to ₹1,440, but the bill charges ₹2,160, ₹720 more. Amount: ₹720.

3. C-reactive protein (CRP) charged 2 times on 2026-09-21 (bill lines 4, 5). Lines 4, 5 charge the same service on the same day at the same price. Unless the test or service was genuinely performed twice, one entry is a duplicate. Amount: ₹700.

Please also share the supporting records or justification for:

- Anaesthesia - General, complex (Grade IV) looks higher-grade than usual (bill line 9). Uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy is typically performed under standard general anaesthesia (Grade II). This bill uses Anaesthesia - General, complex (Grade IV). That can be justified by complications, so ask the hospital for the anaesthesia/procedure record. If it was a standard case, the typical charge is up to ₹12,000. Amount in question: ₹11,000.

Please issue a revised final bill, send it to my insurer's TPA so the settlement can be revised, and refund any excess I have paid.

Yours faithfully,
Meera Krishnan
[Phone] | [Email]
